predecessors.name: Rashtrakuta dynasty
predecessors.text: the Rashtrakuta core and the Deccan seized by Tailapa II in 973

successors.name: Yadava dynasty of Devagiri
successors.text: Kalyani and the northern Deccan: 'conquered the former Chalukya capital Kalyani, and declared himself a sovereign ruler' (Seuna page, 1187)

successors.name: Hoysala Kingdom
successors.text: the southern Karnataka part of the Chalukya country; the Seuna page has the Krishna and Malaprabha as the Yadava-Hoysala border after Soratur

successors.name: Kakatiya dynasty
successors.text: Telangana, held by the Kakatiyas as Cliopatria draws them from 1177

ledger.x: 973: Tailapa II makes the Chalukyas sovereign at the Rashtrakuta capital Manyakheta.
1007: the Cholas invade the Chalukya country.
By 1007: the Lata region passes to the Western Chalukyas.

c. 1008: Durlabharaja takes Lata back. 'He invaded the Lata region, and defeated the Lata Chalukya ruler Kirtiraja' (c. 1008). The page adds that Kirtiraja regained control 'within a short time', undated, and was defeated by Bhoja c. 1018, so the hold may have been brief. Confidence 1 (was 2): the Chaulukya page dates…

c. 1010 (bridge): the southern Deccan leaves the Chalukya shape. Cliopatria removes 608 cells (southern Karnataka and the Andhra country) from 1010 to 1033; the page's 1007 invasion and c. 1020-21 battles with the Cholas are the only related sentences and name no land. Page silent on the year and the land; the Chola…
1018-1020: Bhoja captures upper Konkan.

c. 1020-21: the Chola wars on the southern marches end. 'fought many battles with the Cholas in the south around c. 1020-21.' The page gives no treaty; the Chola dossier closes the Ratta Padi war in 1020 with Maski.
1034 (bridge): the southern strip and the Vengi coast return to the Chalukya shape (521 more cells, to 82.4 E).
1040 (bridge): the 1034 additions leave the shape again, 136,000 km2.
c. 1042: Someshvara I moves the Chalukya capital to Kalyani. 'moved the Chalukya capital to Kalyani in c. 1042.'
1052: Rajadhiraja's second invasion.
1052: the Koppam campaign ends in a Chola victory without annexation.
By 1055: the Chalukyas take upper Konkan from the Paramaras.
1058: the Chalukyas plunder Malwa.
1066: the Chola frontier war reopens.
1067: the plunder of the Paramara cities ends.
1068: the Battle of Vijayawada.
1085: Vikramaditya VI takes Kanchi.
1088: Vikramaditya VI takes parts of Vengi.

c. 1089 (bridge): Kanchi leaves Chalukya hands. 'held it for a few years'; 'Although Kulottunga I subsequently recovered the region, it was later regained by Vikramaditya.' The page gives no year for the loss, so 1089 (four years after 1085) is a confidence-1 bridge.
1093: the contest of 1088 ends with the conquest.
1093: Vengi again.
1099: Vengi lost.
1111 (bridge): 63 more Gujarat cells (Lata proper) enter the Chalukya shape.

c. 1118: Vengi a third time. 'conquered and came under his rule from 1118 to 1124'; the Western Chalukya page: 'reconquered in c. 1118 and held it till 1124'. The Chola dossier records the loss in c. 1118.

c. 1122: the Hoysalas accept Chalukya suzerainty. After battles at 'Goa, Kannegala, Halasur and Hosavidu' (c.1117-1122) Vishnuvardhana 'had to accept Chalukya suzerainty'. The page dates the battles to c.1117-1122 and gives no later year, so 1122 is the last year of the war. Vishnuvardhana had annexed Gangavadi from…
1126 (bridge): Vikramaditya VI dies and the Hoysala tie lapses.
1133: the Cholas retake Vengi.
1157: the Kalachuris take Kalyani.
1163: Telangana leaves the Chalukya shape for the Kakatiyas.
1183: the Kalachuri hold on Kalyani ends.
1187: Bhillama V takes Kalyani.
1187: the Western Chalukya Empire ends.

wars.name: Chola invasions of the Western Chalukya country
Western Chalukya-Paramara wars
wars.outcome: c. 1024: 'Jayasimha II subdued the Paramara of central India' (Western Chalukya page); after 1042 Someshvara I invaded Malwa and sacked Dhara (Paramara and Bhoja pages); the Chalukyas plundered Paramara cities in 1058-1067. No annexation is recorded.

wars.name: Battle of Koppam
wars.outcome: Chola victory (infobox, 28 May 1052; the page also gives 1054 and 1052 'according to Sen'); Rajadhiraja was killed and Rajendra II crowned himself on the field and set up a pillar at Kolhapur.

wars.name: Battle of Vijayawada
wars.outcome: Vikramaditya VI invaded the Chola Empire in 1066 and Someshvara I fought Virarajendra Chola at Vijayawada in 1068; the page names no result.

wars.name: Vikramaditya VI's wars for Kanchi and Vengi
wars.outcome: Kanchi captured in 1085 and held a few years; parts of Vengi contested from 1088; Vengi held 1093-1099 and 1118-1124 (the Chola side takes it back by 1133).

wars.name: Hoysala-Chalukya war
wars.outcome: After the Hoysala victory over the Cholas at Talakad in 1116, battles at 'Goa, Kannegala, Halasur and Hosavidu' (c.1117-1122) ended with Vishnuvardhana accepting Chalukya suzerainty.

wars.name: Chalukya-Kakatiya war of 1149
wars.outcome: The Chalukya ruler 'was defeated by the Kakatiya king Prola in 1149'; no land is named.

wars.name: Kalachuri usurpation of Kalyani
wars.outcome: Bijjala II captured Kalyani in 1157; the Chalukyas, under Someshvara IV, recovered it from 1181-1183.

wars.name: Seuna conquest of Kalyani
wars.outcome: Bhillama V conquered Kalyani in 1187; Someshvara IV was driven into exile at Banavasi in 1189 and the dynasty ended.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey frontier is given by any page opened; the Tungabhadra and Krishna lines against the Hoysalas and Seunas are described but not surveyed, and the Narmada is the rough northern limit.
